calibration.note: 0..10 m = 729.5 px (72.95 px/m); 0..5 m = 365 px (73.0). Plate is 1:100 ('0m01 pour metre'). The bar is horizontal only; vertical scale assumed equal (engraved on one plate, fig. 8/9 beam agree with each other to 1 px).

frame: plate px; fig. 7 bow is LEFT (small x), stern RIGHT. Heights z_m measured up from the keel bottom (fig. 7 py 1427, fig. 9 py 2190).

fig7_profile.sternpost_note: v2 (verifier): the sternpost is a band between two parallel lines ~17 px apart, both raking 16.6 deg (fore line 1802.5@1428 -> 1881@1165, aft line 1820 -> 1898). v1 mixed the aft-line foot with the fore-line top (12.5 deg, wrong). Hull aft edge = aft line. The rudder lies aft of it (after edge 1897@1428 -> 1929@1165).

quarter_gallery_px.note: windowed panel seen in profile; carved bracket below it at py 1145-1180

fig8_half_breadth.note: outer line = rail plan; px from centreline. Bow tip px 235, stern end px 2015 (same x as fig. 7). Lower-curve hits at px 1604-1824 were noisy (waterline crossings) and are left out.

fig9_midship_section.note: outermost section (v2, see points_v1_superseded); z_m above keel bottom, hb_m half-breadth
fig9_midship_section.points_v1_superseded: v1 eye readings from the 2x zoom were 6-8 px too narrow at the bilge (verifier); v2 = mean of both halves from a background-subtracted row scan, y 2010-2170 every 10 px; above z 2.6 m the outer line runs into the frame line at x 980, so those points take the verifier readings (210/213 px at y 1900)
